questions.q: A DFA with 7 states accepts at least one string of length 9. What must be true of its language?
questions.exp: A string of length at least the number of states forces a repeated state, so a loop can be pumped to give infinitely many accepted strings.

questions.q: Which statement correctly compares symmetric and asymmetric encryption?
options: Symmetric uses a public/private key pair; asymmetric uses one shared key
Both use the same key, but asymmetric is faster
Symmetric uses one shared secret key and is faster; asymmetric uses a public/private key pair
Asymmetric encryption needs no keys at all
questions.exp: Symmetric ciphers (DES, AES) share one secret key and are fast; asymmetric ciphers (RSA) use a key pair and suit key exchange and digital signatures.

questions.q: ARP messages are carried directly in
questions.exp: ARP is encapsulated straight in an Ethernet frame (EtherType 0x0806) and is not routed beyond the local network.

questions.q:
What is printed by fun(5)?
void fun(int n){ if(n<=0) return; printf("%d ", n); fun(n-2); printf("%d ", n); }
questions.exp: It prints 5, 3, 1 on the way down, and 1, 3, 5 on the way back.

questions.q: In a 2-input CMOS NAND gate the transistors are arranged as
options: two PMOS in series and two NMOS in parallel
two PMOS in parallel and two NMOS in parallel
two PMOS in parallel (pull-up) and two NMOS in series (pull-down)
questions.exp: The output is 0 only when both inputs are 1, which needs both series NMOS to conduct; the parallel PMOS pull the output high when either input is 0.

questions.q: In the Go-Back-N protocol the receiver window size is:
questions.exp: A Go-Back-N receiver accepts only the next in-order frame, so its window size is 1.

questions.q: Which of the following is the best example of a digital library repository?
options: Shodhganga, the repository of Indian theses
A pen drive without any metadata
questions.exp: Shodhganga (INFLIBNET) is an Indian digital repository of PhD theses.

questions.q: The 8-bit register 10010110 is rotated left by one position (circular shift). The result is
questions.exp: The MSB (1) that is shifted out re-enters at the LSB: 0010110 followed by 1 = 00101101. The logical shift left would put 0 in the LSB.

questions.q: Strassen's algorithm has the recurrence
questions.exp: Seven half-size multiplications plus Θ(n²) additions.

questions.q: An 8051 is driven by a 12 MHz crystal. The duration of one machine cycle is
questions.exp: One machine cycle = 12 oscillator periods = 12 / 12 MHz = 1 microsecond.

questions.q: Which memory in a microcontroller system loses its contents when power is removed?
questions.exp: RAM is volatile; Flash, EEPROM and ROM are non-volatile and hold the firmware.

questions.q: A stack grows toward lower addresses and the stack pointer initially holds 5000. After three PUSH operations of 2-byte values, the stack pointer holds
questions.exp: Each push decrements SP by 2: 5000 - 3 × 2 = 4994.

questions.q: A binary tree with n nodes has how many NULL child pointers? (This is the basis of threaded binary trees.)
questions.exp: Total child pointers = 2n and n-1 are used by edges, leaving 2n - (n-1) = n + 1 null pointers.

questions.q:
Dept(did) = 10, 20, 30; Emp(eid, did) = (1,10), (2,10), (3,30). What does this return?
SELECT did FROM Dept d WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT * FROM Emp e WHERE e.did = d.did);
questions.exp: Departments 10 and 30 have employees. Only department 20 has no matching Emp row, so NOT EXISTS is true for it.

questions.q: In asynchronous data transfer using handshaking, the two units coordinate using
options: A common clock shared by both
Control signals indicating that data is valid and that data has been accepted
questions.exp: Handshaking uses request/acknowledge (data valid / data accepted) signals instead of a shared clock.

questions.q: A topological ordering of a directed graph exists if and only if the graph
questions.exp: A cycle makes it impossible to place all its vertices before their successors; every DAG has an order.

questions.q: When a multivalued attribute of an entity is converted to the relational model, it is represented by
options: a separate relation containing the entity's key and the attribute
questions.exp: A multivalued attribute becomes a new relation with the owner's primary key plus the attribute, one row per value.

questions.q: The recurrence T(n) = T(n/3) + T(2n/3) + n has solution
questions.exp: Each level of the recursion tree costs n and the depth is about log_(3/2) n.

questions.q: Given that Shape is a Java interface, which statement causes a compile-time error?
questions.exp: An interface cannot be instantiated directly; arrays of an interface type and null references are fine.

questions.q: Which of the following is an international standard for Electronic Data Interchange?
questions.exp: UN/EDIFACT (and ANSI X12 in the USA) are EDI message standards.

questions.q: A branch instruction located at address 2000 uses PC-relative addressing. The PC has already been incremented by 4 and the offset is -12. The branch target address is
questions.exp: Target = PC + offset = 2004 - 12 = 1992.

questions.q: Making the constructor of a C++ class private prevents:
options: Creating objects of the class from outside the class
questions.exp: Only members or friends can then construct objects; this is used in the Singleton pattern.

questions.q: The IEEE 830 recommended practice deals with
questions.exp: IEEE Std 830 gives recommended practice for writing an SRS.

questions.q: Statement I: The Waterfall model easily accommodates changes in requirements late in development. Statement II: Prototyping helps in clarifying requirements. Which is correct?
options: Statement I is false and Statement II is true
Statement I is true and Statement II is false
questions.exp: Waterfall is rigid and handles late change poorly, whereas prototypes elicit user feedback that clarifies requirements.

questions.q: What is the correct order of messages in DHCP address assignment?
questions.exp: The DORA sequence is Discover, Offer, Request, Acknowledge.

questions.q: The time taken by the dispatcher to stop one process and start another running is called:
questions.exp: Dispatch latency is the time for the dispatcher to perform the context switch and resume a process.

questions.q: Which of the following sorting algorithms has a worst-case time complexity of O(n log n)?
questions.exp: Heap sort guarantees O(n log n) in all cases, whereas quick sort degrades to O(n²).

questions.q: Priority inversion happens when:
options: a high-priority process waits for a lock held by a low-priority process that is preempted by a medium-priority process
a low-priority process always runs before higher ones
priorities are assigned in decreasing order
questions.exp: The medium-priority process indirectly delays the high-priority one; priority inheritance is the usual fix.

questions.q: In 4-queens with queens already placed at (row 1, column 2), (row 2, column 4), (row 3, column 1), the column of the queen in row 4 that gives a solution is
questions.exp: Columns 1, 2 and 4 are used; column 3 is not diagonal-attacked by any previous queen.

questions.q: R(A, B) = {(1,x), (2,y)} and S(B, C) = {(x,p), (z,q)}. How many tuples of R left outer join S contain a NULL?
questions.exp: The result is (1,x,p) and (2,y,NULL). Only the tuple for (2,y) has a NULL, so 1.

questions.q: How many pointer fields are there in total in a circular doubly linked list with n nodes (each node has a prev and a next pointer)?
questions.exp: Every node has two pointer fields, giving 2n.

questions.q: Which declaration uses an unbounded wildcard in Java generics?
questions.exp: The ? symbol is the unbounded wildcard type argument.

questions.q: The uncompressed size of 10 seconds of audio sampled at 8 kHz with 8 bits per sample and one channel is
questions.exp: 8000 samples/s × 1 byte × 1 channel × 10 s = 80,000 bytes.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
x = 10
def f():
    x = 20
    def g():
        print(x)
    g()
f()
print(x)
questions.exp: g sees f's x (enclosing scope) which is 20; the global x stays 10.

questions.q: After the third consecutive collision in Ethernet, a station chooses a random wait multiplier K from:
questions.exp: After the nth collision K is chosen from 0 to 2ⁿ − 1; for n = 3 this is 0 to 7.

questions.q: LSD radix sort requires the intermediate digit-wise sort to be
questions.exp: Digits are sorted from least to most significant; stability preserves the order produced by earlier (lower) digits.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
print("Hello"[1:3] + "World"[-3:], "ab" < "b", "Z" < "a", [1, 2] < [1, 3])
questions.exp: Slices give 'el' and 'rld'; strings compare by character code, so 'ab'<'b' and 'Z'<'a'; lists compare element-wise.

questions.q: In a 4-bit 2's complement system, the bit pattern 1000 represents
questions.exp: The MSB has weight -2³ = -8, so 1000 = -8.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
print(list(zip([1, 2, 3], 'ab')), dict(zip('xy', [1, 2])), list(enumerate('pq', 1)))
questions.exp: zip stops at the shortest input; enumerate with start=1 numbers from 1.

questions.q: The JAM trinity, used for direct benefit transfer in India, stands for:
questions.exp: JAM links Jan Dhan bank accounts, Aadhaar identity and mobile numbers.

questions.q: Transaction T1 runs SELECT COUNT(*) FROM P WHERE age > 30 twice. In between, T2 inserts a new row with age 40 and commits, so T1 sees different counts. This anomaly is called
questions.exp: A phantom read occurs when a repeated range query returns new rows inserted by another committed transaction.

questions.q: The padlock symbol and 'https' in a browser's address bar indicate that:
options: The website is owned by the government
Data between browser and server is encrypted using TLS/SSL
The computer is free of viruses
questions.exp: HTTPS uses TLS/SSL to encrypt communication.

questions.q: Software Quality Assurance (SQA) activities are applied
options: Only to the final source code
questions.exp: SQA is a process-wide umbrella activity covering reviews, standards, audits and testing at all phases.

questions.q: What happens if run() is called directly on a Thread object instead of start()?
options: The body of run() executes in the calling thread like an ordinary method
questions.exp: Only start() creates a new thread of execution; run() alone is a normal method call.

questions.q: Which of the following helps reduce power consumption in a data centre?
options: Running every server at idle continuously
Installing more standalone physical servers for each application
questions.exp: Virtualization lets fewer physical servers run many workloads, saving power.

questions.q: The Optimal page replacement algorithm is not practical because it:
options: needs knowledge of future page references
questions.exp: It replaces the page that will not be used for the longest time, which cannot be known in advance; it serves as a benchmark.

questions.q: Which pair of functions satisfies f(n) = o(g(n)) (little-o)?
options: f(n) = n, g(n) = n log n
questions.exp: Only n/(n log n) → 0; the other pairs have ratio tending to a nonzero constant or infinity.

questions.q: Which organisation develops and maintains the CSS specifications?
questions.exp: The World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) publishes the CSS standards; IETF handles HTTP RFCs.

questions.q: A model that is too simple and has high bias typically suffers from
questions.exp: High bias means the model cannot capture the data pattern, giving poor training and test performance.

questions.q: In PHP, which statement includes a file and stops the script with a fatal error if the file cannot be found?
questions.exp: require produces a fatal error on failure; include only gives a warning.

questions.q: The "naive" assumption of the Naive Bayes classifier is that
options: features are conditionally independent given the class
the data contains no missing values
questions.exp: Independence given the class lets the likelihood be written as the product of P(xi | class).

questions.q: Converting a 2NF relation to 3NF involves eliminating
options: transitive dependencies of non-prime attributes on the key
questions.exp: 2NF already removes partial dependencies; 3NF removes transitive dependencies of non-prime attributes on candidate keys.

questions.q: Which of the following is a technique for requirements validation?
questions.exp: Requirements validation checks that the SRS reflects customer needs using reviews, walkthroughs, prototyping and test-case generation.

questions.q: A RISC program executes 1.3 × 10⁹ instructions with CPI 1.2; the equivalent CISC program executes 10⁹ instructions with CPI 3. Both run at the same clock rate. How many times faster is the RISC version?
questions.exp: Cycles: RISC = 1.56 × 10⁹, CISC = 3 × 10⁹; speedup = 3 / 1.56 ≈ 1.92.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
import numpy as np
a = np.arange(1, 13).reshape(3, 4)
print(a.shape, a[:, 1], a.sum(axis=0))
questions.exp: Column 1 holds 2,6,10; axis=0 sums down each column to 15,18,21,24.

questions.q: Deterministic and nondeterministic Turing machines are equivalent in
options: the class of languages they accept
the space used for every language
questions.exp: Any NTM can be simulated by a DTM, though possibly with exponential slowdown.

questions.q: The language { a^n b^m | n ≠ m } is:
questions.exp: A grammar can generate more a's than b's or more b's than a's, but a finite automaton cannot compare counts.

questions.q: An 8-bit serial-in shift register is clocked at 1 MHz. The time needed to load an 8-bit word serially is
questions.exp: One bit per clock pulse of period 1 μs: 8 × 1 μs = 8 μs.

questions.q: The Linux kernel is classified as:
options: a monolithic kernel with loadable modules
questions.exp: Linux runs most services in kernel space but supports dynamically loadable modules.

questions.q: Which function is best suited to read a whole line of text (including spaces) from the keyboard safely into a character array?
questions.exp: fgets reads up to a newline including spaces and limits the characters read to the buffer size.

questions.q: In a write-back cache, the dirty bit of a line indicates that
options: The block was modified after being loaded and must be written to memory before being replaced
The block is locked in the cache
The block has never been accessed
questions.exp: Write-back defers memory updates; the dirty bit marks lines needing a write-back on eviction.
null matches both overloads; the compiler picks the most specific type, String.

questions.q: A generator function g contains exactly two yield statements. What happens after it = g(); next(it); next(it); next(it) is executed?
options: The first value is returned again
questions.exp: Each next() resumes the generator to its next yield. After both yields are consumed, the third next() raises StopIteration.

questions.q: A browser trusts a website's TLS certificate mainly because it
options: Is signed by a trusted CA whose root certificate is in the browser's trust store
questions.exp: Trust is chained from the site certificate up to a root CA that the browser already trusts.

questions.q: A simple (non-circular) array-based queue of size 5 has A, B, C, D, E enqueued, then two dequeues are done, and finally enqueue(F) is attempted. What happens?
options: Overflow is reported although two slots at the front are free
F replaces the element at the front
The queue shifts automatically and stores F
questions.exp: rear is already at the last index, so a linear queue reports overflow; a circular queue would avoid this.

questions.q: When converting a context-free grammar into an equivalent PDA that accepts by empty stack, the minimum number of PDA states needed is
options: equal to the number of variables
questions.exp: The standard construction uses a single state, with the stack simulating leftmost derivations.

questions.q: Router X is 2 hops-cost away from neighbour Y. Y advertises a distance of 5 to network Z. X currently has a distance of 9 to Z. After applying the distance vector update, what is X's distance to Z?
questions.exp: New cost via Y = 2 + 5 = 7, which is less than 9, so X updates to 7.

questions.q: In multiple-granularity locking, an intention-exclusive (IX) lock on a table means that the transaction
options: intends to set exclusive locks on some rows within the table
has locked the whole table exclusively
only wants to read the table
questions.exp: IX indicates an intention to take X locks at a finer level (rows) below this node; it does not itself lock the whole table.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a symmetric-key algorithm?
questions.exp: RSA is an asymmetric (public-key) algorithm; the others use one shared key.

questions.q: Which statement about FileNotFoundException in Java is correct?
options: It is an unchecked exception that extends RuntimeException
It is an Error thrown only by the JVM
It is thrown only by the Scanner class
It is a checked exception and a subclass of IOException
questions.exp: FileNotFoundException extends IOException, which extends Exception, so it is checked: it must be caught or declared. It is thrown by FileReader, FileInputStream, Scanner(File) and others.

questions.q: Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) in a microcontroller is commonly used to
options: control motor speed or LED brightness
questions.exp: Varying the duty cycle of a fixed-frequency pulse varies the average power delivered to a motor or LED.

questions.q: C-SCAN is preferred over SCAN because it:
options: provides a more uniform waiting time
questions.exp: C-SCAN services requests in one direction and returns quickly, so cylinders at either end are treated more fairly.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
print(6 & 3, 6 | 3, 6 ^ 3, 1 << 4, ~5, 17 >> 2)
An inverted index used by search engines maps:
options: each IP address to a domain
each URL to its file size
each term to the list of documents containing it
questions.exp: An inverted index stores, for every word, the documents (and positions) where it occurs.

questions.q:
Statement I: REST is an architectural style rather than a protocol.
Statement II: SOAP messages can be transported only over HTTP.
Which is correct?
questions.exp: SOAP is protocol-independent and can run over SMTP, TCP etc., so Statement II is false.

questions.q: A merge conflict in Git occurs when:
options: a branch name is longer than 40 characters
the same lines of a file were changed differently in the branches being merged
the remote repository has been deleted
questions.exp: Git cannot decide automatically between conflicting edits; the developer resolves them and commits.

questions.q: Which is the strongest sign that an e-mail link is a phishing attempt?
options: The e-mail arrived in the morning
The link's domain differs from the organisation it claims to represent
questions.exp: A mismatched or look-alike domain is a classic phishing indicator.

questions.q:
Match the SQL statements with their categories.
1. CREATE  2. INSERT  3. GRANT  4. COMMIT
P. DCL  Q. TCL  R. DDL  S. DML
questions.exp: CREATE is DDL, INSERT is DML, GRANT is DCL and COMMIT is TCL.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following algorithm?
a = 48, b = 18
while b != 0
  t = b
  b = a mod b
  a = t
print a
questions.exp: This is Euclid's algorithm: gcd(48, 18) = gcd(18, 12) = gcd(12, 6) = gcd(6, 0) = 6.

questions.q: The function F(A, B, C, D) = Σm(0, 2, 5, 7, 8, 10, 13, 15) simplifies to
questions.exp: Corners (0, 2, 8, 10) give B'D' and the centre block (5, 7, 13, 15) gives BD, so F = B ⊙ D.

questions.q: Assuming P ≠ NP, which statement must be true?
options: No NP-complete problem can be solved in polynomial time
Every problem in NP is in P
SAT can be solved in polynomial time
questions.exp: If any NP-complete problem were in P, then P = NP.

questions.q: A combinational circuit with 3 inputs and 4 outputs is to be implemented using a ROM. The required ROM size (words x bits) is
questions.exp: 3 inputs give 2^3 = 8 address combinations (words) and the 4 outputs are the data bits, so an 8 x 4 ROM.

questions.q: Which set of 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi channels (20 MHz wide) are non-overlapping?
questions.exp: Channels 1, 6 and 11 are spaced at least 25 MHz apart and do not overlap.

questions.q: The expression A'B'C + A'BC + ABC' + ABC simplifies to
questions.exp: A'C(B' + B) + AB(C' + C) = A'C + AB.

questions.q: In C, for the declaration int a[10], the expression a[3] is equivalent to
questions.exp: Array indexing is defined as pointer arithmetic: a[i] is *(a + i).

questions.q: Which of the following problems is undecidable?
options: Whether a given DFA accepts a given string
Whether a given CFG generates a given string
Whether a given regular expression matches the empty string
Whether a given Turing machine halts on a given input
questions.exp: The halting problem is the classic undecidable problem; the others are decidable.

questions.q: Why is a random salt added to a password before hashing it?
options: To allow the password to be decrypted later
To defeat precomputed (rainbow table) attacks and make identical passwords hash differently
questions.exp: Per-user salts force attackers to attack each hash separately.

questions.q: In an 8086 with SS = 3000H and SP = 0100H, PUSH AX is executed. At which physical address is AH stored?
questions.exp: SP becomes 00FEH; the high byte AH is stored at SP+1 = 00FFH (physical 300FFH) and AL at 300FEH.

questions.q: Which phase of a compiler is executed first?
questions.exp: Lexical analysis converts the source text into tokens and precedes syntax analysis, semantic analysis and code generation.

questions.q: What is the number of states in the minimal complete DFA over {0,1} that accepts strings containing 101 as a substring?
questions.exp: States track the matched prefix of 101 (ε, 1, 10) and a final trap state after 101: 4 states.

questions.q: Evaluate the prefix expression: / + 9 3 - 8 2
questions.exp: Scanning from the right: 8-2=6; 9+3=12; 12/6=2.

questions.q: Embedded operating systems are typically characterized by:
options: small memory footprint and a fixed dedicated function
questions.exp: They are designed for devices such as appliances and controllers with limited resources.

questions.q: Which is the first fundamental step in digital image processing?
questions.exp: The process begins with acquiring the image; enhancement, restoration, compression and segmentation follow.

questions.q: A relationship set that involves three entity sets is called a
questions.exp: The degree of a relationship set is the number of participating entity sets: 1 = unary, 2 = binary, 3 = ternary.

questions.q: The serial I/O lines of the 8085 are
questions.exp: SID (serial input data) and SOD (serial output data) are used with the RIM and SIM instructions.

questions.q: Which section of the IT Act empowers the government to intercept, monitor or decrypt information in the interest of national security?
questions.exp: Section 69 authorises interception, monitoring and decryption of information through any computer resource under stated conditions.

questions.q: In the many-to-one multithreading model, which is a major drawback?
options: Thread creation requires a kernel call
Each user thread needs a kernel thread
If one thread makes a blocking system call, the entire process blocks
questions.exp: All user threads map to one kernel thread, so a blocking call blocks all of them and there is no parallelism on multiprocessors.

questions.q: Which technique allows many hosts with private addresses to share a single public IPv4 address?
questions.exp: Network Address Translation rewrites private addresses (and ports) to a public address at the border router.

questions.q: Which relationship is best modelled using inheritance?
questions.exp: Inheritance models an is-a relationship.

questions.q: e-PG Pathshala provides:
questions.exp: It is a UGC-MHRD initiative for e-content at the postgraduate level.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an example of operant behaviour?
options: A pigeon pecking a key for food
A student raising a hand to get attention
A rat pressing a lever for water
Salivating at the sound of a bell after conditioning
questions.exp: Salivation is a reflex controlled by antecedent stimuli, which is respondent (classical) behaviour.

questions.q: Learning that occurs without reinforcement and remains hidden until a reward appears is called
questions.exp: Tolman's rats formed cognitive maps without reward.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a component of curriculum?
questions.exp: The usual components are objectives, content, learning experiences and evaluation.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): A test can be reliable without being valid.
Reason (R): Reliability only ensures consistency, not that the right trait is measured.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
Both A and R are true and R explains A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.exp: Consistent measurement of the wrong thing is reliable but invalid.

questions.q: Raven's Progressive Matrices is considered a
questions.exp: It uses patterns rather than language, reducing cultural bias.

questions.q: In Freud's psychosexual theory, the Oedipus complex appears in the
questions.exp: The phallic stage (3-6 years) involves attachment to the opposite-sex parent.

questions.q: Assertion (A): Piaget's theory is called a constructivist theory. Reason (R): It holds that children actively build their knowledge through interaction with the environment. Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R explains A
Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.exp: Constructivism views learners as active builders of knowledge, exactly as Piaget described.

questions.q: According to Vygotsky, 'tools of intellectual adaptation' include
options: language, counting systems and symbols of the culture
questions.exp: Cultural tools such as language and number systems mediate thinking.

questions.q: Tagore received the Nobel Prize for literature in
questions.exp: Tagore won it for Gitanjali in 1913.

questions.q: After a first microteaching session, the trainee should:
options: modify the lesson using the feedback and teach it again
give a test to the pupils
questions.exp: Re-plan and re-teach follow feedback in the cycle.

questions.q: Vivekananda's view of the teacher-student relationship is based on
options: the Gurukul ideal of close personal contact
questions.exp: He favoured students living close to a character-building teacher.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a desirable quality of a teacher?
questions.exp: Teachers must be open to new ideas.

questions.q: Kohlberg's theory extended the earlier work on moral judgment of
questions.exp: Kohlberg built on Piaget's stage approach to moral thinking.

questions.q: The Kothari Commission (1964-66) famously said that
options: the destiny of India is being shaped in her classrooms
questions.exp: This is the opening line of its report.

questions.q: Which of the following best expresses the view of modern psychology on heredity and environment?
options: Development results from continuous interaction between heredity and environment
questions.exp: Heredity sets potentials while environment determines how far they are realised; both interact.

questions.q: Teaching-learning material (TLM) is listed in the lesson plan so that:
options: the aids needed are decided and arranged in advance
questions.exp: Advance planning ensures aids are available and well used.

questions.q: Which of the following assessment tasks best tests the practical skills in CS?
options: Writing the definition of a compiler
Writing and running a program to solve a given problem
questions.exp: Executing a program shows application ability.

questions.q:
Statement I: Formative evaluation is a continuous process.
Statement II: Summative evaluation is generally conducted at the end of a term or course.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statements I and II are false
Both Statements I and II are true
questions.exp: Formative is ongoing; summative is terminal.

questions.q: The 'Holistic Progress Card' proposed in NEP 2020 will:
options: show only the marks of the final exam
give a 360-degree view of the learner's progress including self- and peer-assessment
questions.exp: It records cognitive, affective and psychomotor development.

questions.q: For resolving a quarrel between two students, the best method is
questions.exp: Conflict resolution skills encourage responsible behaviour.

questions.q: The body that monitors the implementation of the RTE Act at the national level is the
options: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
questions.exp: Section 31 gives monitoring powers to NCPCR and State commissions.

questions.q: Which is the correct sequence of the maxims 'known to unknown' used for teaching a new CS topic?
options: Start with the most advanced topic and go backward
Link the new topic to what students already know and then extend it
Begin with the unknown and then revise the known
questions.exp: Using prior knowledge as the starting point is the 'known to unknown' maxim.

questions.q: 'Level of aspiration' refers to
options: the goal a person sets for future performance
questions.exp: It is the standard a person tries to reach in a task, often shifting after success or failure.

questions.q:
Statement I: Action research begins with identifying a problem in one's own practice.
Statement II: Action research is conducted only by external experts.
Choose the correct option.
questions.exp: The teacher-practitioner identifies and investigates the problem.

questions.q: Slow learners are usually those with an IQ in the range of about:
questions.exp: Slow learners are below average but not mentally disabled.

questions.q:
Statement I: Audio-visual aids can make abstract ideas easier to understand.
Statement II: Audio-visual aids should be used only at the end of a lesson.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statements I and II are true
Both Statements I and II are false
questions.exp: Aids are used wherever they help understanding, not only at the end.

questions.q: The 'stem' of a multiple-choice question is:
options: the question or incomplete statement presented to the learner
questions.exp: The stem poses the problem; options follow.

questions.q:
Match the method with its proponent:
P. Project method
Q. Heuristic method
R. Dalton Plan
S. Kindergarten system
questions.exp: Kilpatrick - project; Armstrong - heuristic; Parkhurst - Dalton; Froebel - kindergarten.

questions.q: The Remote Associates Test, designed to assess creative thinking, was developed by
questions.exp: Mednick's RAT asks for a word linking three apparently unrelated words.

questions.q: Which Gupta ruler is called the 'Napoleon of India' by V. A. Smith?
questions.exp: Samudragupta's many conquests, recorded in the Allahabad Pillar inscription, earned him the title.

questions.q: Which Indian city is popularly called the 'Pink City'?
questions.exp: Jaipur's old city was painted pink in 1876 to welcome the Prince of Wales.

questions.q: What is the state bird of Bihar?
questions.exp: The house sparrow was declared the state bird of Bihar.

questions.q: Who administers the oath of office to the President of India?
questions.exp: Under Article 60, the oath is administered by the Chief Justice of India or the senior-most judge available.

questions.q: Mining, fishing and agriculture belong to which sector of the economy?
questions.exp: The primary sector extracts natural resources directly from nature.

questions.q: The Kanwar Lake (Kabartal) wetland, a Ramsar site, is located in which Bihar district?
questions.exp: Kabartal (Kanwar Jheel) in Begusarai was designated a Ramsar site in 2020.

questions.q: The soil conservation method of ploughing along the contour lines of a slope helps to
options: Reduce soil erosion by slowing run-off
questions.exp: Contour ploughing creates barriers to run-off, retaining water and soil.

questions.q: Which of the following is a perpetual (inexhaustible) resource?
questions.exp: Solar energy is available continuously and is not depleted by use; groundwater, forests and soil are renewable only if managed.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a method of in-situ conservation?
questions.exp: A seed bank stores seeds outside the natural habitat and is therefore ex-situ.

questions.q: A major difference between a National Park and a Wildlife Sanctuary is that in a National Park
options: Private ownership of land is encouraged
Human activities such as grazing and forestry are not permitted
questions.exp: National parks have stricter protection with no grazing or collection of forest produce.

questions.q: Of 70 students, 40 play cricket, 30 play football and 10 play neither. How many play both games?
questions.exp: Students playing at least one = 60; both = 40 + 30 - 60 = 10.

questions.q: An arc of a circle subtends an angle of 80° at the centre. What angle does it subtend at a point on the remaining part of the circle?
questions.exp: The angle at the centre is double the angle at the circumference, so 80°/2 = 40°.

questions.q: A cyclist rides at 16 km/h. How far will he travel in 45 minutes?
questions.exp: 45 minutes = 0.75 h; distance = 16 x 0.75 = 12 km.

questions.q: The population of a village (in hundreds) was 40, 46, 55 and 60 in 2019, 2020, 2021 and 2022. What is the percentage increase from 2019 to 2020?
questions.exp: Increase = 6 on 40, so (6/40) x 100 = 15%.

questions.q: A learner knows 7 x 4 = 28 but cannot find 7 x 8. Which teaching strategy best uses prior knowledge?
options: Ask the learner to memorise the whole table by rote
Tell the learner to look the answer up
Skip the topic until next year
Show that 7 x 8 is double 7 x 4, i.e. 2 x 28 = 56
questions.exp: Linking new facts to known ones (doubling) builds understanding and number sense.

questions.q: What is the sum of the alphabet positions of all the vowels in the word EDUCATION?
If the value of a word is the sum of the alphabet positions of its letters, which of the following words has the value 30?
questions.exp: FACT = 6 + 1 + 3 + 20 = 30. NAME = 33, MEAL = 31 and HEAL = 26.

questions.q: A month of 30 days begins on a Saturday. How many Sundays does the month have?
questions.exp: 30 days = 4 weeks + 2 extra days (Saturday and Sunday). So Sunday occurs 5 times.

questions.q: If P means '+', Q means '×' and R means '−', then 8 Q 3 P 10 R 6 = ?
Five books P, Q, R, S and T are stacked one on another. P is above Q but below R. S is at the bottom. T is between R and P. Which book is second from the top?
questions.exp: From top to bottom: R, T, P, Q, S. The second from the top is T.
